From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Thanks Alyssa — answering inline and adding tech notes.

> 1) JSON schema compliance: strictly by JSON Schema?
We run a two-step verification: 
- First-pass: JSON Schema validation (required fields, types, regex where appropriate). This is the 99% compliance target.
- Second-pass: lightweight semantic checks (normalization rules, enum lookups, custom regex for SKU patterns). We report both metrics. For your SKU shape we recommend adding a normalization hook in the post-processor to canonicalize dashes/case before asserting enum membership.

> 2) Retries / dedupe
Recommendations: 
- Use an idempotency key generated by your service (e.g., request_uuid + input_checksum). Redwood will pass that through tool-call metadata and include it in logs.
- Backoff: exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 attempts for transient 5xx/timeout.
- On success, the function should return a canonical event id we persist; on client-side retries we ignore duplicates by checking the canonical id.
- To reduce duplicates for streaming outputs, include a finalization marker in the callable response so downstream consumers can safely commit.

> 3) Security / KV cache encryption
- Hosted: logs are redacted by default (we redact things that look like SSNs, credit card numbers, and emails unless you opt-in to share).
- Dedicated / Private: KV cache can be configured to use your KMS; at rest encryption is supported. Audit logs are available with the Dedicated plan and can be exported to your S3.

Technical attachments I added to the Drive:
- function_signatures.md — recommended function signatures + example return payloads (we include the canonical event id field and last_update timestamps).
- example_prompt_set.json — includes negative/edge examples and the prompt templates we used for the benchmark.
- schema_v1.json — schema with comments on fields we expect to be brittle.

Model guidance for the evals (practical notes)
- RedWave-7B-q4: preferred for the first smoke test — expected median latency ~120ms @ p99 batching off for short prompts. Good cost baseline.
- LlamaX-13B-qlo: better extraction precision for nested fields; expect ~2–2.5x token cost and ~1.8x latency. Use for regression checks and for the 8/2 run.
- Warmup: do a 500–1k warmup to populate KV cache for repeated SKUs — that materially reduces latency variance.

Validation checklist (we'll run these):
- Schema validation pass rate (schema_v1)
- Semantic normalization error rate (lower is better)
- Field-level precision/recall for SKU attributes
- Function-calling end-to-end idempotency test (simulate duplicate requests)
- Retry/backoff fault-injection (network drop, timeouts)

I'll run the smoke test with RedWave-7B-q4 Monday morning and share the logs; Ben/Rishi — I'll add a short readout doc to the Drive afterwards.
